hero.headline: Treasury moves to cut off crypto exchange MEXC from U.S. financial system over alleged $16 billion in illicit transactions
hero.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department moved to cut off cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over allegations the platform processed $16 billion in illicit transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia. The action targets MEXC Global for alleged sanctions violations.

The Treasury decision blocks MEXC from accessing U.S. financial infrastructure and conducting transactions with American counterparties. The enforcement measure represents one of the largest actions against a cryptocurrency exchange based on alleged illicit transaction volume.

The alleged $16 billion in flows involve transactions connected to sanctioned countries including Iran, North Korea and Russia. The Treasury did not specify the time period over which the transactions allegedly occurred or detail the nature of the illicit activity.

In response to the Treasury action, digital asset company NatGold Digital announced it would immediately delist its NATG token from MEXC. The move reflects the immediate market consequences for platforms cut off from the U.S. financial system.

cards.headline: Congress demands answers on Nvidia CEO's reported ties to alleged Chinese spy
cards.teaser: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged

Chris Coons pledged an investigation, while a group of House Republican committee chairs requested a briefing from Huang by November 11 to determine whether U.S. national security has been compromised.

cards.headline: US intelligence memo alleges Chinese state security recruited tech executive to spy on Nvidia CEO
cards.teaser: A memo reportedly claims China's Ministry of State Security recruited a Singapore company executive to gather intelligence on Jensen Huang.
cards.body:
A U.S. intelligence memo circulated earlier this year alleged that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to media reports. The memo, first reported by The New York Times, also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang.

An Nvidia spokesperson said Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were not unusual and that the company does not share classified information with customers. The reports come amid scrutiny of chip export controls, including concerns that a Chinese company authorized to buy advanced Nvidia chips may be operating as a front for a blacklisted firm.

cards.headline: AI tools are enabling automated hacking at scale, upending the cybersecurity industry
cards.teaser: Artificial intelligence systems are now enabling attackers to automate the entire hacking process in real time, fundamentally disrupting the cybersecurity industry built over the p
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence systems are now enabling attackers to automate the entire hacking process in real time, fundamentally disrupting the cybersecurity industry built over the p

Open-weight AI models have advanced to the point where they can automatically identify software vulnerabilities, write exploits, and break into targets simultaneously, collapsing what was traditionally a multi-step process requiring teams of skilled hackers. Stamos described a wave of breaches in recent weeks affecting major technology companies, including a chain of attacks that began with a compromise of Fireworks, an AI services provider.

A series of bomb threats targeting airlines and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure across Europe has disrupted everyday life and heightened security concerns, though the perpe

The incidents have affected multiple sectors, including aviation, healthcare, and food supply systems. Cyberattacks targeted European refrigeration systems and critical health infrastructure, including a French blood bank.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Postal Service restrictions on mail-in ballot delivery
cards.teaser: A federal judge has blocked a proposed restriction on mail-in voting across the United States, preventing the Postal Service from implementing a plan that would have denied ballots
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked a proposed restriction on mail-in voting across the United States, preventing the Postal Service from implementing a plan that would have denied ballots to voters in states refusing to turn over their voter rolls to the federal government.

Judge Emmet Sullivan of the US District Court for the District of Columbia ruled against the restriction, marking the second time that a plan to limit mail ballots across the country has faced a court setback.

The blocked restriction stemmed from an order targeting mail-in voting access. Civil rights groups, including the NAACP, challenged the proposed changes in court, arguing that the Postal Service directive would create barriers to voting. Multiple organizations joined the legal challenge, contending that the restrictions would make it harder for Americans to cast ballots by mail, particularly affecting communities that depend heavily on mail-in voting.

Mail-in voting has become a significant method of casting ballots in recent election cycles, with millions of Americans relying on the option. Voting rights advocates had opposed the proposed changes, saying they would create unnecessary obstacles for voters without good cause.

The judge's order keeps current mail ballot handling procedures in place while the case continues through the courts. The ruling ensures that existing practices for delivering mail ballots remain unchanged for now, preventing the implementation of the proposed restrictions.

The decision represents a significant setback for efforts to limit mail-in voting access. Judge Sullivan found sufficient grounds to block the restriction, siding with those who argued the changes would harm voting access.

This case is part of a broader legal battle over voting access and election administration that has intensified in recent years. As states prepare for upcoming elections, courts continue to weigh competing claims about voting methods and election security. The block demonstrates ongoing judicial skepticism toward restrictions on mail-in voting, with multiple courts now rejecting similar proposals.

The outcome comes amid heightened focus on election procedures and voting access. Legal challenges to voting restrictions have become common in the current political environment, with courts frequently called upon to determine the constitutionality of various election administration policies.

The Postal Service has not yet announced whether it will appeal the ruling. If appealed, the case could move to higher courts, potentially reaching the appellate level. The decision ensures that the current mail ballot system continues operating under existing rules while legal proceedings advance.

The ruling highlights how courts are actively shaping election policy through litigation. As voting access remains a contested issue, this decision will likely influence other ongoing legal battles over mail-in voting procedures and voter eligibility requirements across the country.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

hero.headline: Gunman kills one, wounds five in shooting in central Israel
hero.teaser:
Shooting at Louisiana Mardi Gras Parade Wounds Five, Including Child

A shooting during a Mardi Gras parade in Clinton, Louisiana on Saturday left five people wounded, including a
hero.body:
Shooting at Louisiana Mardi Gras Parade Wounds Five, Including Child

A shooting during a Mardi Gras parade in Clinton, Louisiana on Saturday left five people wounded, including a six-year-old child, authorities said. The incident occurred shortly after the midday start of the Mardi Gras in the Country parade.

East Feliciana Sheriff Jeff Travis told reporters that three people carrying firearms were taken into custody at the scene, though investigators had not yet determined whether they were involved in the shooting. Louisiana State Police took over the investigation following the incident.

Chief Criminal Deputy Bill Cox from the sheriff's office said all five victims were expected to survive, though specific details about their conditions were not immediately released. The sheriff's office appealed to the public for assistance, asking anyone who photographed or recorded the shooting or nearby areas to share that material with investigators.

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry responded to the shooting on social media, describing it as "absolutely horrific and unacceptable" and calling for prayers for the victims.

Clinton, a town of approximately 1,300 people located in the metropolitan area surrounding Baton Rouge, Louisiana's capital, has now been the site of a significant shooting incident during what should have been a community celebration.

The shooting comes as gun violence continues at high rates across the United States. According to the nonpartisan Gun Violence Archive, at least 24 mass shootings had occurred in the country by the time of the Louisiana incident. The archive defines a mass shooting as an incident in which four or more victims are wounded or killed.

The persistent occurrence of mass shootings in America has prompted calls from many quarters for Congress to implement stricter gun control measures. However, lawmakers have historically shown reluctance or inability to pass meaningful legislation addressing the issue, despite ongoing public pressure and repeated incidents of gun violence.

The investigation into the Clinton parade shooting is ongoing as authorities work to determine the circumstances of the incident and establish whether the three people taken into custody had any involvement in the violence that unfolded during the community event.

cards.headline: Israeli president tasks Eisenkot with forming government after inconclusive election
cards.teaser: Opposition leader has 28 days to build a coalition after securing more lawmaker endorsements than Netanyahu.
cards.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government, passing over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Herzog announced the decision Saturday after 67 lawmakers endorsed Eisenkot following the October 27 election, in which neither side secured a majority. Only 46 backed Netanyahu.

Eisenkot, a former army chief who leads the Yashar party, has 28 days to assemble a coalition of at least 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. His four-party alliance won 48 seats in the election, while Netanyahu's bloc secured 53. If Eisenkot fails, Herzog will nominate another candidate or a new election will be called.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.

Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.headline: Gunman kills six in attack on Krakow's main square, three more bodies found at his home
cards.teaser: At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday afternoon, and police later found three bodies at his home. The a
cards.body:
At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday afternoon, and police later found three bodies at his home. The a

The attacker, identified as a 25-year-old Polish man, drove into Krakow's Main Market Square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car. Armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes, preventing further casualties.

hero.headline: Six killed in shooting in Krakow, Poland; British citizen among dead
hero.body:
A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

The 25-year-old Polish suspect, described by Poland's interior minister as having been fascinated by far-right ideologies and holding ultra-nationalist views, was injured in a shootout with police and taken to hospital for surgery. One police officer was critically injured in the firefight and a second suffered less serious injuries. Poland's prime minister called the officers heroes and said they saved many lives.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three additional bodies were found during a search of the suspect's home about 125 miles from Krakow. Tusk said there were strong indications the two women and one man were the suspect's immediate family members. More weapons and ammunition were found in a car belonging to the suspect, who wore military tactical gear during the attack but was not a member of the Polish armed forces.

Of the 15 people injured in the attack, five were foreign nationals from Britain, Austria, Russia, Germany, and Portugal. The attack began shortly before 3 p.m. local time and lasted about three minutes as the attacker drove through the historic city center, firing at shops, a tram, and pedestrians before crashing and engaging police. Krakow has declared a period of mourning through November 11.

cards.headline: Norris takes pole in wet Brazilian qualifying, hopes for rain in Sunday's race
cards.teaser: Lando Norris secured pole position at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in extremely wet conditions that halted qualifying for nearly 90 minutes.
cards.body:
Lando Norris took pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after qualifying in what he described as some of the wettest conditions he has driven in. The session was stopped for nearly 90 minutes because conditions were deemed too dangerous, with drivers reporting zero visibility and aquaplaning at speeds exceeding 120 mph.

Norris said he hoped for rain in Sunday's race, acknowledging his McLaren lacked pace in dry conditions. George Russell qualified second but was frustrated by a team miscommunication he felt cost him pole. Grid penalties for several front-runners produced an unfamiliar starting order, with Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen starting 20th and 21st after engine replacements.

cards.headline: Wisconsin state trooper detained by ICE released under supervision after intervention by DHS secretary
cards.teaser: A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air
cards.body:
A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air

Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney. Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher.

cards.body:
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix after power-unit changes resulted in penalties for both

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also face grid penalties, with Leclerc dropping 10 places and Russell five. Hamilton initially faced a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season.

cards.headline: Tech stocks fall below S&P 500 valuation for first time since 2017
cards.teaser: The technology sector traded at 17 times expected earnings this week, below the broader index's 18 times, as chip stocks led a fifth straight losing week.
cards.body:
The technology sector traded at 17 times expected earnings this week, below the broader index's 18 times, as chip stocks led a fifth straight losing week.

Technology stocks in the S&P 500 traded at about 17 times expected earnings this week, below the broader index's 18 times for the first time since 2017, according to Truist Wealth. The sector fetched 32 times at its October 2025 peak.

cards.headline: Musk says SpaceX could buy legacy telecom carrier, move telecom stocks
cards.teaser: Elon Musk said SpaceX could acquire a legacy carrier and use its spectrum more effectively, sending SpaceX shares up 8.6% while telecom stocks dipped.
cards.body:
Elon Musk told investors on November 6 that SpaceX could buy a legacy telecom carrier and use its airwaves ten times more effectively, though he named no target. He made the comment by video at the Baron Investment Conference in New York. SpaceX rose 8.62 percent to $134.27, while Verizon and AT&T each slipped 0.89 percent.

Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Hoettges said on a November 5 earnings call that SpaceX would need at least 200 billion euros, or about $220 billion, to compete with established U.S. carriers. His company controls T-Mobile. SpaceX bought AWS-4 and H-block spectrum licenses from EchoStar in September 2025 for roughly $17 billion and has agreed to buy nationwide 800 MHz licenses.

cards.teaser: The action targets alleged flows linked to Iran, North Korea, and Russia.
cards.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department moved to cut off cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over alleged illicit transactions totaling $16 billion. The action targets transactions allegedly linked to Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

The Treasury's enforcement action bars MEXC from accessing U.S. financial infrastructure over alleged sanctions violations. At least one digital asset issuer announced it would immediately delist from the exchange following the Treasury action.

cards.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas next year, Musk says
cards.teaser: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the
cards.body:
Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the

Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the trucks entirely or shift production elsewhere, but said the decision was to make room for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars. Wes Morrill, the project's lead engineer, wrote on social media that Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab, appearing to suggest the vehicle is being discontinued.

cards.headline: Scientists find two massive tears in Arabian tectonic plate beneath Iran
cards.teaser: The ruptures offer rare insight into how oceans close and continents collide.
cards.body:
Scientists have discovered two giant tears in the Arabian Plate beneath southeastern Iran, caused by contrasting rock densities within the plate. One section consists of dense oceanic basalt being pushed underground, while another section is lighter continental rock that resists subduction and forms mountains. The mismatch is creating the ruptures, according to research published in Nature Geoscience.

Researchers used 69 seismic monitoring stations to detect the tears: one horizontal rupture where the Zagros collision zone meets the Makran subduction zone, and a smaller vertical tear near the Makran Trench. The tears have been progressing for millions of years and may eventually merge, providing geologists a rare view of the transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision.

cards.headline: Phone makers expand lineup of child-focused devices with monitoring and restricted access
cards.teaser: Companies offer smartphones and landlines designed for kids, featuring limited internet access and parental controls amid safety concerns.
cards.body:
As parents increasingly worry about unrestricted smartphone access for children, companies are developing devices specifically for kids with heavily modified software that removes or restricts web browsers, social media, and app stores. Products like the Bark Phone and Pinwheel run on smartphone hardware but allow parents to approve contacts, monitor locations, set screen time limits, and receive alerts for cyberbullying or explicit content through companion apps.

Other companies take a minimalist approach with calling-and-texting-only devices or home phones designed for children. Gabb phones eliminate online risks entirely with no browser or app store, while devices like Tin Can and Ooma MyPhone function as landlines with approved-contact-only calling. Pricing ranges from $68 for basic landlines to $240 for monitoring-enabled smartphones, with monthly service fees starting around $8 to $35.

cards.headline: NASA opens public sign-up to send names to Titan aboard Dragonfly rotorcraft
cards.teaser: The agency will inscribe names on a chip during spacecraft assembly for the mission launching in 2028.
cards.body:
NASA opened public registration in late October for people to submit their names to fly aboard Dragonfly, a nuclear-powered rotorcraft mission to Saturn's moon Titan. The names will be inscribed on a chip during the spacecraft's assembly, with submissions closing in January. The agency plans to launch Dragonfly in 2028, with the vehicle scheduled to arrive on Titan's surface in 2034.

The SUV-sized rotorcraft will fly between locations on Titan to study the moon's organic-rich landscape and search for conditions that could support life. Dragonfly will operate for approximately 3.3 Earth years, making one flight every Titan day, which lasts about 16 Earth days.

cards.headline: PC RAM capacities decline for first time as 16 GB gains on 32 GB and 64 GB configurations
cards.teaser: CPU-Z validator data shows systems with 16 GB of RAM climbing to 33% of submissions as higher-capacity configurations shrink.
cards.body:
Data from CPU-Z validator submissions shows PC RAM capacities declining year over year for the first time, according to one of the software's developers. Systems with 32 GB of RAM remain most common at 37.2% but dropped 2.5 percentage points from a year ago, while 64 GB fell 18% to 7.3%. Configurations with 16 GB climbed 12.9% to 33.0%, and 8 GB rose 5.5% to 11.0%.

The shift coincides with rising memory prices, with manufacturer Team Group expecting shortages to worsen between the fourth quarter of 2026 and second quarter of 2027. DDR4 platforms also gained ground, reaching 54.5% of submissions as DDR5 slipped to 32.9%. The validator data reflects only user-submitted systems over three months.

cards.headline: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Runs on Jailbroken PS5 and iPhone After Switch 2 Launch
cards.teaser: Two days after Nintendo released the remake on Switch 2, developers ported it to modified PlayStation 5 consoles and iPhones using emulation.
cards.body:
Nintendo's Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, which launched on Switch 2 on November 5, is now running on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles and iPhones. Developer Vampinity posted results showing the game loading on a modified PS5 at 15 to 20 frames per second before running out of memory, calling it nowhere near playable. The emulator port uses shader work borrowed from PC emulator forks.

Developer Joe Jiang demonstrated the game running on an iPhone 17 Pro Max by compressing memory usage to 3.4 gigabytes, below the 8,192 megabyte limit for iOS apps. Jiang said his method could bring any Switch or Switch 2 game to iOS, Android, and other mobile platforms but has not yet released the software.

hero.headline: Oregon routs Ohio State 41-28, likely ending Buckeyes' playoff hopes with fake punt sparking turnaround
hero.body:
Oregon defeated Ohio State 41-28 in Columbus, likely extinguishing the Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes and marking the first time Ohio State has suffered three or more losses by November 7 since 2011. The Ducks rallied from a 14-0 deficit to score 41 unanswered points after a fourth-down fake punt deep in their own territory completely shifted momentum late in the first half.

Facing fourth-and-9 from their own 31-yard line while trailing 14-3, Oregon coach Dan Lanning called for a fake punt. Linebacker Teitum Tuioti found a wide-open Matayo Uiagalelei for a 30-yard gain. The Ducks scored a touchdown five plays later, then capitalized on a Luke Fahey interception to take a 17-14 halftime lead despite trailing 14-3 with less than two minutes remaining in the half. Oregon never looked back, scoring 28 consecutive points at one point—the most unanswered points Ohio State has allowed since Wisconsin scored 39 straight in 1999.

Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola completed 25 of 40 passes for 257 yards and two touchdowns after struggling early. Running back Dierre Hill Jr. added two touchdowns, including a 48-yard score in the third quarter. Ohio State quarterback Luke Fahey, a freshman, completed 13 of 19 passes for 143 yards and an interception in the first half but struggled to maintain rhythm after the hot start. Star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught a late touchdown but the game was already out of reach.

Ohio State now stands at 6-3 with no ranked opponents remaining on the schedule. The Buckeyes entered the game already on the playoff bubble and drop to 35.7 percent playoff odds according to forecasting models. The loss came in what was considered a must-win game for a program that began the season with national championship aspirations.

cards.headline: No. 1 Miami faces No. 11 Notre Dame in top-15 college football showdown
cards.teaser: The top-ranked Hurricanes put their national ranking on the line against the Fighting Irish in Week 10.
cards.body:
No. 1 Miami faces No. 11 Notre Dame in a Week 10 college football game with the Hurricanes' top national ranking at stake. The matchup represents one of the weekend's highest-profile contests between ranked teams.

The game adds another chapter to a rivalry previously defined by seven memorable contests. Notre Dame held a lead over Miami during the game, according to live scoring updates.

cards.headline: NFL handbook language grants Commissioner broad discretion over Brandon Aiyuk reinstatement as 49ers seek bonus repayment
cards.teaser: League has delayed action on wide receiver's reinstatement request since late October amid dispute over up to $13 million.
cards.body:
The NFL Player Personnel Handbook grants Commissioner Roger Goodell apparently unlimited discretion over reinstatement applications from players on the reserve/left squad list, according to league interpretation now shaping wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's case. The league has delayed action on Aiyuk's request since October 27 as the San Francisco 49ers seek reimbursement of up to $13 million in previously paid bonus money.

The Collective Bargaining Agreement contains no provisions governing the reserve/left squad list, potentially placing the matter within management rights beyond union challenge. The NFL Players Association has remained silent throughout the process, which appears to tie Aiyuk's return to his willingness to repay the disputed amount to San Francisco.

cards.headline: Lando Norris takes pole for Sao Paulo Grand Prix in rain-disrupted qualifying
cards.teaser: The McLaren driver secured his third consecutive pole in Brazil after qualifying was stopped for 90 minutes due to dangerous conditions.
cards.body:
Lando Norris took pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after a rain-delayed qualifying session that was halted for nearly 90 minutes due to dangerous conditions. Mercedes driver George Russell qualified second, with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg filling the second row.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start 20th and 21st after taking engine penalties for exceeding their seasonal allowance. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who qualified fourth, also faces a 10-place penalty for engine usage. Sunday's forecast calls for light rain at the Interlagos circuit.

cards.headline: Chev Clarke stops Chris Billam-Smith in seventh round for first career stoppage loss
cards.teaser: Clarke handed the former cruiserweight world champion the first stoppage defeat of his professional career in their all-British non-title fight.
cards.body:
Chev Clarke stopped former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith in the seventh round Saturday, handing him the first stoppage loss of his professional career. Clarke knocked Billam-Smith down with a right hand early in the seventh, then floored him again moments later with a barrage of punches before the referee intervened despite Billam-Smith's protests.

The win improved Clarke's record to 13-2 and inflicted a third professional defeat on Billam-Smith, who previously lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019. Clarke also defeated Billam-Smith in the amateur ranks a decade ago.

cards.headline: Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame ceremony draws criticism after teammate's explicit anecdote
cards.teaser: A former linebacker's story about adult toys and Aaron Hernandez prompted backlash during Saturday's induction event outside Gillette Stadium.
cards.body:
Rob Gronkowski's induction into the New England Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday outside Gillette Stadium took an uncomfortable turn when former linebacker Niko Koutouvides recounted an explicit story from 2011 training camp. Koutouvides told attendees, including children, about Gronkowski discussing adult toys with Aaron Hernandez during their second season, prompting Gronkowski to put his head in his hands and quickly end the speech.

Social media users criticized the story as inappropriate and questioned why Koutouvides was given a speaking role. One user called the speech "horrendous," while others noted few people recognized the former player. Gronkowski cut off Koutouvides immediately after he finished, saying "Thank you very much, you're done."

cards.headline: Willy Hutchinson upsets Joshua Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title in Manchester rematch
cards.teaser: Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rema
cards.body:
Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rema

The judges scored the rematch 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 in favor of Hutchinson, making the 28-year-old Scot the first British champion at the weight since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. The bout was elevated from an interim title fight to a full championship after American David Benavidez vacated the belt to move up to cruiserweight.

hero.headline: Sylvester Stallone says his 20-year rivalry with Arnold Schwarzenegger ended when Schwarzenegger ran for California governor
hero.body:
Sylvester Stallone said his decades-long rivalry with Arnold Schwarzenegger only concluded when Schwarzenegger left acting to run for governor of California. In a recent interview on "The Rest Is Entertainment" podcast, Stallone recounted how the two action stars competed throughout the 1980s and 1990s as both sought to dominate the emerging action film genre.

Stallone said the tension began early in their careers when both actors recognized they were vying for leadership in action cinema. He recalled noticing Schwarzenegger at the Golden Globe Awards, where the two exchanged hostile looks. The competition extended both on and off screen, with Stallone making films like "Rambo" while Schwarzenegger countered with "Commando." Stallone described the rivalry as "very contentious" but added that he enjoyed the challenge.

Even when the two partnered on the restaurant chain Planet Hollywood in 1991, Stallone said they would not appear on stage together to give speeches. The hostility persisted for two decades until Schwarzenegger decided to pursue political office.

Stallone said the rivalry finally ended when the two encountered each other at a cigar lounge around the time Schwarzenegger launched his gubernatorial campaign. Stallone told him they were no longer in competition because Schwarzenegger was leaving the film industry. He thanked Schwarzenegger for motivating him throughout their careers, and Schwarzenegger expressed similar sentiments. Stallone said the two remain friendly today and still competitive by nature, though no longer financially competitive.

cards.headline: Animation director denies AI use in Dior ad, cites automated interpolation tool
cards.teaser: Sylvain Chomet and producer Aton Soumache respond to viral speculation about the hand-drawn holiday campaign.
cards.body:
Animation director Sylvain Chomet and producer Aton Soumache denied that generative AI was used in a Dior holiday advertisement that had been promoted as hand-drawn. Soumache told Variety that the ad was created over seven months by 20 artists, including six animators, and acknowledged using "an automated interpolation system for a very small part of the process." The filmmakers did not identify the software or specify how much of the production involved interpolation.

The advertisement's original announcement described it as hand-drawn using techniques from the 1940s. Viral speculation had pointed to visual irregularities including extra fingers and morphing objects as possible evidence of AI generation. Chomet attributed those elements to established animation techniques involving exaggerated shapes to convey movement.

cards.headline: Pokemon anime studio unveils AI coloring tool trained on three hand-painted frames
cards.teaser: OLM developed the tool under a Japanese government-backed research project that wrapped in February.
cards.body:
OLM, the Japanese animation studio behind the Pokemon anime series, has developed an AI coloring tool that learns a show's visual style from just three hand-painted frames, according to board director Yotsukura Tatsuo. The tool emerged from a 15-month research project under GENIAC, a generative AI program overseen by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry that concluded in February.

An artist colors three frames by hand, and the system learns the show's line shapes and color palette in about 90 seconds, then colors each remaining frame in around 15 seconds. At proof-of-concept stage, Yotsukura estimated the tool has cut painting workload by around 30 percent, though checkers who review colored frames have somewhat more work.

cards.headline: Bill Skarsgård says he wasn't considered for James Bond role but would play a villain
cards.teaser: The Swedish actor told a podcast he wasn't asked to audition for Denis Villeneuve's Bond reboot.
cards.body:
Bill Skarsgård said he was not asked to audition for the James Bond role in Denis Villeneuve's upcoming reboot, joking that producers may have ruled out a Swedish actor for the part. Speaking on the "Happy Sad Confused" podcast, Skarsgård said he was never "thrown into the mix" while British and Australian actors tested for the role.

Skarsgård said he would be open to playing a Bond villain in the style of Mads Mikkelsen's character, though he added he is becoming more selective about villain roles after playing Pennywise, Count Orlok, and other antagonists. He said any future villain role would need to feel original and different from his previous work.

cards.headline: 'Heated Rivalry' Season 2 in Production With 6 Episodes, Third Season Unconfirmed
cards.teaser: Creator Jacob Tierney confirmed the six-episode count for the second season, while the show's Canadian streamer declines to confirm speculation about additional projects.
cards.body:
Creator Jacob Tierney confirmed that "Heated Rivalry" Season 2 will consist of six episodes, matching the first season's count. Tierney told Andy Cohen last month that production would be complete by year's end, though he did not specify what the shoot encompasses.

Canadian streamer Crave, which produces the series, said it has no projects to confirm. Speculation about back-to-back seasons began after recurring guest star Dylan Walsh mentioned filming 12 episodes in an August video, comments he later suggested got him in trouble. The series streams on HBO Max in the United States.

cards.headline: Jodie Sweetin says she had $190 in bank account before filming 'Fuller House'
cards.teaser: The actress revealed she had to borrow money during her first week on the Netflix reboot after years of financial struggles.
cards.body:
Jodie Sweetin said she had $190 in her bank account when she began filming the 2016 Netflix reboot "Fuller House," revealing she had to borrow money during her first week on set. The actress, who played Stephanie Tanner on the original sitcom "Full House," disclosed her financial struggles on the "We're Still Here, Babe" podcast, saying none of her co-workers knew of her situation at the time.

Sweetin, who has been open about past addiction struggles, said those habits left her with no money at one point and led her to take non-Hollywood jobs to support her children. "Fuller House" ran for five seasons on Netflix from 2016 to 2020, reuniting most of the original cast.

cards.headline: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani Meets Puerto Rican Band Chuwi in San Juan
cards.teaser: The meeting during the annual Somos Conference focused on gentrification, displacement, and how music spreads awareness of Puerto Rico's struggles.
cards.body:
The meeting during the annual Somos Conference focused on gentrification, displacement, and how music spreads awareness of Puerto Rico's struggles.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani met with Puerto Rican band Chuwi in San Juan on Friday during the annual Somos Conference, where New York State lawmakers engage with Latino advocates. The musicians, who gained international fame collaborating with Bad Bunny and recently released their debut album Libertad addressing government corruption and colonial policies, discussed gentrification and displacement affecting both Puerto Rico and New York's Puerto Rican communities.

hero.headline: Federal judge blocks Postal Service restrictions on mail-in ballot delivery
hero.teaser: A federal judge has blocked a proposed restriction on mail-in voting across the United States, preventing the Postal Service from implementing a plan that would have denied ballots
hero.body:
A federal judge has blocked a proposed restriction on mail-in voting across the United States, preventing the Postal Service from implementing a plan that would have denied ballots to voters in states refusing to turn over their voter rolls to the federal government.

Judge Emmet Sullivan of the US District Court for the District of Columbia ruled against the restriction, marking the second time that a plan to limit mail ballots across the country has faced a court setback.

The blocked restriction stemmed from an order targeting mail-in voting access. Civil rights groups, including the NAACP, challenged the proposed changes in court, arguing that the Postal Service directive would create barriers to voting. Multiple organizations joined the legal challenge, contending that the restrictions would make it harder for Americans to cast ballots by mail, particularly affecting communities that depend heavily on mail-in voting.

Mail-in voting has become a significant method of casting ballots in recent election cycles, with millions of Americans relying on the option. Voting rights advocates had opposed the proposed changes, saying they would create unnecessary obstacles for voters without good cause.

The judge's order keeps current mail ballot handling procedures in place while the case continues through the courts. The ruling ensures that existing practices for delivering mail ballots remain unchanged for now, preventing the implementation of the proposed restrictions.

The decision represents a significant setback for efforts to limit mail-in voting access. Judge Sullivan found sufficient grounds to block the restriction, siding with those who argued the changes would harm voting access.

This case is part of a broader legal battle over voting access and election administration that has intensified in recent years. As states prepare for upcoming elections, courts continue to weigh competing claims about voting methods and election security. The block demonstrates ongoing judicial skepticism toward restrictions on mail-in voting, with multiple courts now rejecting similar proposals.

The outcome comes amid heightened focus on election procedures and voting access. Legal challenges to voting restrictions have become common in the current political environment, with courts frequently called upon to determine the constitutionality of various election administration policies.

The Postal Service has not yet announced whether it will appeal the ruling. If appealed, the case could move to higher courts, potentially reaching the appellate level. The decision ensures that the current mail ballot system continues operating under existing rules while legal proceedings advance.

The ruling highlights how courts are actively shaping election policy through litigation. As voting access remains a contested issue, this decision will likely influence other ongoing legal battles over mail-in voting procedures and voter eligibility requirements across the country.

cards.teaser: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'

Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night after Trump blamed her for the election results in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump will install Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, in the position starting Monday.
